style.layout: phone-mockup product launch: centred phones (upright and tilted 3D), big centred headlines above or beside the device, UI fragments used as floating cards; one dark 3D phone-array sequence

style.ui_highlight: UI shown as full phone screens or as isolated white cards with soft shadow; toggle switches animate to show customisation; no cursor, no spotlight, no zoom ring
style.text_animation: headlines slide/fade word by word, letters fill in, red colour accent on one keyword, giant single-word beats
style.pacing_frames: 8 shots avg 165 frames, min 21, max 293; calm, roughly one idea every 4-5 s
style.real_ui_vs_motion: real app screens composited into motion-designed phone mockups and 3D scenes; UI is static screenshots animated as layers, not screen recording
style.audio: audio stream present (opus); edits land on soft beats
style.three_beat: yes: problem (frames 0-287) -> product/customisation demo (frames 287-1123) -> outcome + CTA (frames 1123-1320)

verdict: Classic app-launch structure: cold open on the problem, phone-mockup feature beats, App Store CTA and logo end card (sheet_1-3).
Light airy palette (white to pale blue gradient, navy text, blue accent) with two contrasting dark 3D sequences for energy.
UI is real but composited: screenshots inside phone mockups, feature rows extracted as white cards with shadows, toggles animated to show the customisable claim.
Pacing is moderate: 8 shots in 44 s, most holds 100-300 frames, one 21-frame flash; readable for a 30 s demo.

Useful lessons: isolate a UI row as a floating card to explain one feature, use a single giant word as a breather beat, end on a store-card CTA; avoid the heavy 3D phone arrays which need a 3D pipeline.
